equity_bridge.item: H1-2026 unlevered owner FCF already realised in the 2026-06-30 net debt
equity_bridge.note: Q2-2026 6-K: FCF C$1,842M less C$84M Newmarket land sale, C$68M SBC and C$8M award withholding = C$1,682M levered; plus after-tax interest paid C$503M x 0.75 = C$377M -> ~C$2,059M unlevered. Year 1 (FY2026) projects these six months again.
FY2025 XBRL EquityMethodInvestments; their income is in Other income, outside the flows

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (1.9% 5yr, 0.3% 3yr) is >30% below EPS (8.6% 5yr) and revenue (4.6% 5yr): CN returns essentially all earnings via dividends plus C$2-4.7B/yr of buybacks, so book value does not compound and is not a usable growth anchor (same pattern as Visa). The 5yr revenue CAGR starts from the FY2020 COVID trough; the 10yr revenue CAGR of 3.2% is selected as the through-cycle anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding; no interest income adjustment, CN is net debt): FY2020 3,190; FY2022 3,810; FY2023 3,663; FY2024 3,024; FY2025 3,276 (C$M). FY2021 is not in the CSV (only equity extracted). The owner and reported FCF CAGRs are near-identical - SBC is ~0.6% of revenue and not growing faster than cash flow. FCF has fallen since FY2022 because capex rose from 16% to 21% of revenue; that capacity build is what the FY2026 capex step-down reverses. FY2017 EPS includes the US tax-reform deferred-tax gain and FY2023 EPS a land-sale gain.

scenario_narratives.base: CN keeps its half of the Canadian rail duopoly and its three-coast single-line network earns inflation-plus pricing on low-single-digit volume growth. FY2026 lands near the raised guidance (+6% revenue, inflated by fuel surcharge), FY2027 is soft as fuel normalises, the US-Canada tariff dispute grinds on without a cross-border collapse, and the TCRC contract expiring Dec-2026 is settled through the usual CIRB/arbitration route with a short or no stoppage. Margins recover to the FY2022-25 peak of ~50% pre-SBC rather than beyond it, and capex settles at 17.5% of revenue once the FY2023-25 capacity build is done.
scenario_narratives.bull: Intermodal truck-to-rail conversion through Prince Rupert and the Gulf, LNG Canada and grain/fertiliser export growth push volumes above GDP; PSR productivity and record fuel efficiency carry the pre-SBC margin to ~51.5%; the USMCA review de-escalates tariffs; and the lower capex run-rate holds at ~17% because the capacity is already built. Growth of 4.5-5% through FY2031 fading to 3.5%, terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 50% US tariffs on Canadian goods (effective Aug-2026) hit the ~32% of revenue that is cross-border traffic, fuel surcharge reverses, and a 2027 TCRC stoppage repeats the August-2024 lockout: FY2027 revenue falls 2% and the margin drops to 46% (FY2024 lockout year was 48.2% pre-SBC). Regulatory pressure on the duopoly (interswitching, CTA rate oversight) caps pricing, volumes grow only ~2%, and capex has to stay at 18.5% for safety rules and network resilience after wildfire/flood outages.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A railway duopoly is about as durable as an operating business gets, so the question is not survival but what the market is paying for it. On an unlevered owner-FCF basis with SBC expensed, capex normalised to mid-cycle and a CAD-built 7.25% WACC, the scenarios are valued in CAD and converted to USD at the dated spot rate. The model gives the network credit for inflation-plus pricing and a return to peak margins, but not for margins beyond the prior peak or for the trapped pension surplus.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value dominates: a 20x cap on base terminal FCF; each 1x of terminal multiple is worth roughly US$4-5/share
Capex normalisation: every 1pp of revenue in mid-cycle capex is ~C$180M/yr of FCF
US-Canada tariffs on the ~32% cross-border book and the Dec-2026 TCRC expiry are front-loaded in years 1-2
FX: the USD-quoted value moves one-for-one with CAD/USD (rate dated 2026-10-03) independent of operations
Pension surplus (C$5.6B) excluded - upside if it ever becomes accessible via contribution holidays or plan changes

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE:CNI, USD); 52-week range 90.74-131.55. Parity-checked against CNR.TO and CAD=X (see inputs.fx_note).
data_sources.financials: CNI_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, CAD despite the USD label) for FY2007-FY2025; SEC companyfacts XBRL for FY2025 SBC, withholding, leases, debt detail and cash taxes; Q2-2026 6-K (a2026q2fsnotes.htm, a2026q2pressreleasestatssu.htm, filed 2026-07-24) for the 2026-06-30 balance sheet, share count, H1 cash flow and raised guidance - saved to research/CNI/Extracted/.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-06-30: 604.9M common shares outstanding (607.6M at 2026-03-31 + 0.2M options exercised - 2.9M repurchased, Q2-2026 statement of changes in equity) + 1.0M dilutive effect of stock-based compensation (Q2-2026 Note 7). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count too would charge it twice. CN is an active repurchaser (C$2,059M FY2025, C$1,337M H1-2026, NCIB up to 24M shares to Feb-2027), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 SEC XBRL (40-F/6-K): AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense C$106M + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation C$9M = C$115M. CN publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. Charged in full although part of CN's awards are cash-settled (already inside OCF) - a deliberate small conservatism (~0.05% of revenue).
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements are CAD (SEC XBRL unit tags are CAD; the CSV/core_metrics 'USD' currency label is the build_facts_xbrl.py hardcode bug). Quote is NYSE:CNI in USD. Model->quote rate CAD->USD 0.7019 = 1/1.4247, Yahoo CAD=X (USD/CAD) at 2026-10-03T21:00Z. Parity check against the TSX primary listing: US$119.77 x 1.4247 = C$170.64 vs CNR.TO C$170.66 at 2026-10-02 close, a 0.01% tie that confirms the rate, its direction and the quote basis. All per-share values are computed in CAD and converted; CN's own 2026 planning assumption is US$0.71 per C$. The rate is not moved by refresh_price.py - refresh it with the price.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CAD, the flows' currency. Cost of equity 8.0% = Government of Canada 10y ~3.4% + beta ~0.9 x 5.0% ERP. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.3% (TTM interest expense C$936M / ~C$21.6B average debt), 3.2% after a ~25.5% blended tax rate. Market weights at C$170.66 x 605.9M = C$103.4B equity vs C$22.3B debt (82/18) give 7.1%; set at 7.25% for a duopoly railway with moderate cyclicality. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. US GAAP: operating lease cost (C$160M FY2025) sits inside operating expenses, so it is already inside EBITDA; the C$465M of operating lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases (C$5M) are inside total_debt. lease_cost_pct_path left at 0 because the charge is already in the margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: None material - CN reports no non-controlling interest.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing: non-US cyclical operating company -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). CN is a Class I freight railway with a duopoly network, US GAAP reporting in CAD, no bank/REIT/holdco features. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). FY0 = FY2025 (revenue C$17,304M); year 1 = FY2026, anchored to the Q2-2026 raised guidance (low-single-digit RTM, mid-to-high single-digit adj EPS growth, capex ~C$2.8B net of reimbursements). Balance sheet and share count are the Q2-2026 6-K (2026-06-30): total debt C$22,254M (current 512 + long-term 21,742), cash C$280M (restricted C$14M excluded). DATA FLAG: the CSV TotalDebt of C$22,107M for FY2025 double-counts the current portion - XBRL LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsIncludingCurrentMaturities is C$21,206M. Not used here. MID-CYCLE: FY2023-25 capex ran 19-21% of revenue during a capacity build; FY2026 guidance steps it down ~C$500M. Capex is normalised to 17.5% of revenue (above D&A of ~11.2% to fund volume growth and inflation in replacement cost) rather than carrying either the 21% peak or the 15.6% guided trough forward. EBITDA margin is pre-SBC (FY2025: (operating income 6,587 + D&A 1,938 + SBC 106) / 17,304 = 49.9%); H1-2026 ran 47.8% as fuel-surcharge revenue (WTI US$80-110) diluted the margin. Cash tax is unlevered (on EBIT): book rate 24.6%, cash rate below book by the accelerated-depreciation deferral, so 21% ramping to 23% as capex intensity falls toward D&A. Pension: the C$5.6B pension surplus (contributions to the DB plan prohibited) and the C$0.46B pension/OPEB liabilities are both left out of the bridge, and the ~C$0.5B/yr non-cash 'other components of net periodic benefit income' is out of the flows - charged consistently once; the trapped surplus is upside not credited. BUYBACKS: C$2,059M FY2025 cash; value-neutral here because SBC is expensed and the count held flat. BRIDGE ITEM: H1-2026 unlevered owner FCF (~C$2.0B) already reduced the 2026-06-30 net debt, yet year 1 projects all of FY2026, so it is deducted once in equity_bridge to avoid counting it twice.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +6.0%: H1 +5.3%, Q2 +11% on 5% RTM growth plus fuel surcharge at WTI US$80-110; H2-2025 base C$8,629M grown ~7%. FY2027 +2.5% as the fuel surcharge normalises, tariffs bite and the TCRC agreement is renegotiated. Then 3.5% (low-single-digit volume + inflation-plus pricing) fading to 3.0%, in line with the 3.2% 10yr revenue CAGR.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA margin: FY2022 50.5%, FY2023 50.4%, FY2024 48.2% (lockout), FY2025 49.9%, H1-2026 47.8%. FY2026 48.5% on fuel-diluted revenue, recovering to 50.0% - the prior peak, not above it.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 cash property additions ~C$3.05-3.1B (H1 C$1,134M at FY2025's 36% H1 seasonality), ~17% of revenue; guided C$2.8B is net of customer reimbursements. Mid-cycle 17.5% thereafter, between the guided trough and the FY2023-25 capacity-build peak of 19-21%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: two dated, binary risks sit inside the first two forecast years - the 50% US tariffs live since Aug-2026 on ~32% cross-border revenue, which management calls the single biggest risk, and the TCRC agreement expiring 31-Dec-2026 under a labour regime that produced a full network stoppage in 2024. Base 50% because Q2-2026 beat-and-raise shows the core franchise intact. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs tariff de-escalation, above-GDP volume and margins beyond the prior peak all at once.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
